human.problem: Cards 5, 6, 8, 9 and 11 name the poet as the speaker of Lamentations 2:20-22 ("the poet speaks straight to God," "In his prayer, the poet asks," "his young men and maidens," "the ones he nurtured and reared"). The text doesn't say who speaks. Verses 18-19 call on Zion to cry out to the Lord for her children, and "those I nurtured and reared" (2:22) may be Zion's own voice. The docs pull two ways here. "Leave open what the text leaves open" says to leave the speaker unstated. "Who's speaking" says to name who is speaking before quoting an "I."
human.question: When the text leaves the speaker of an "I" passage open, as in Lamentations 2:20-22, should Papa Dorin name a speaker, such as the poet or the Daughter of Zion? Or should he quote it without naming anyone, for example "Then comes a prayer: 'Look, O LORD…'"?
